title.bn: অ্যারে ও linked নোড দিয়ে stack বানানো

summary.en: Implement push, pop and peek with explicit empty/full results, then use a stack to match nested brackets.
summary.bn: অ্যারে ও linked নোডে push, pop, peek বানাও এবং stack দিয়ে জোড়া bracket ঠিক আছে কি না দেখো।

sections.title: The latest unfinished job stays on top
Use count as the next free array position
Keep the same operations with linked nodes
Compare the abstraction across storage choices
Use the top to enforce nesting order
Understand constant-time operations and bounded memory
Test the empty and full transitions explicitly
Preserve the abstraction at the boundaries

examples.title: Keep peek non-destructive while pop removes the latest value
examples.explanationHtml: The count names the next free index, so the top element is at count minus one only when count is positive. Peek preserves count. Pop returns twenty before ten, demonstrating last-in, first-out order.

examples.title: Use linked nodes without imposing an array capacity
examples.explanationHtml: Each push allocates one node at the head; pop unlinks and frees that node. The linked version can still fail allocation, so it is not an unlimited stack. Cleanup handles an already-empty owner safely.

examples.title: Match nested brackets by comparing the most recent opener
examples.explanationHtml: Correct counts alone are insufficient: ([)] crosses nesting order. Each closing bracket must match the most recent unmatched opener. The checker ignores non-bracket characters; it is not a C lexer and does not interpret quotes or comments.

examples.title: Reject array overflow and preserve an output on underflow
examples.explanationHtml: The ninth push fails before writing outside the eight slots. A failed pop does not invent a value or modify the output. Status and data stay separate, so zero would remain a valid stored value.

practice.title: Reverse a bounded integer sequence through a stack
practice.statementHtml: Read n from 0 through 8 and n integers from -100 through 100. Push all values, then print each popped value on its own line. Missing or invalid input prints invalid. Input tokens fit int. Do not print a partial reversal before all values have been accepted.
hints: Only pop for output after the complete input succeeds.

practice.title: Check one line of bracket nesting
practice.statementHtml: Read one line with at most 80 characters, excluding its newline. Print balanced when its (), [] and {} are properly nested; print invalid otherwise. Ignore other characters. A blank line is balanced; a missing line is invalid. This is a character exercise, not parsing a programming language.
hints: The final stack must be empty.

practice.title: Trace a push/pop sequence
practice.statementHtml: Trace push 4, push 7, pop, push 9, peek, pop, pop. Give the returned values and explain why peek does not create a second 9.
hints: Write the stack from bottom to top after each operation.
practice.answerHtml: The first pop returns 7, leaving [4]. Push 9 gives [4,9]. Peek returns 9 without changing that sequence. The next pops return 9 and then 4. Peek observes an existing element; it neither removes nor duplicates it.

practice.title: Choose between array and linked storage
practice.statementHtml: Compare a known maximum nesting depth with an unknown growing workload. Include memory and failure behavior.
hints: Both representations can reject an operation.
practice.answerHtml: A bounded array gives predictable storage and no per-push allocation, suitable when the maximum is known. A linked stack grows one allocation at a time but pays pointer/allocation overhead and can fail when allocation fails. Both need explicit failure results. Neither representation changes the LIFO abstraction.

quiz.prompt: Which element does a stack pop first?
options: The most recently pushed remaining element
quiz.explanation: LIFO describes insertion order rather than numeric order.

quiz.prompt: With count as the next free index, where is a nonempty array top?
What must push check before an array write?
quiz.explanation: A full stack has no free element slot.

options: Peek leaves the stored sequence unchanged

quiz.prompt: Why is ([)] invalid despite equal opening and closing counts?
options: The closing order crosses the required nesting
quiz.explanation: The first closer must match the most recent unmatched opener.

quiz.prompt: Can linked_push fail without a fixed capacity?
What must linked_pop do with its removed allocation?
options: Unlink it and free it after saving the value
quiz.explanation: The remaining chain stays owned by top.

quiz.prompt: Which value is removed after two array pushes?
quiz.explanation: The top index becomes one and holds nine; one element remains.

quiz.prompt: Does reading the top change the count?
quiz.explanation: A read-only top observation leaves count at two.

quiz.prompt: How many unmatched openers remain after reading (()?
quiz.explanation: Two openers and one closer leave one unmatched opener; full matching also checks order.

keyPoints.en: A stack exposes last-in, first-out behavior independently of storage.
keyPoints.bn: Storage যাই হোক, stack-এ শেষে ঢোকা মান আগে বের হয়।

keyPoints.en: Keep array count between zero and capacity.
keyPoints.bn: অ্যারে stack-এর count শূন্য থেকে capacity-এর মধ্যে রাখো।

keyPoints.en: Peek observes the top without removing it.
keyPoints.bn: Peek দিয়ে ওপরের মান দেখো; সেটি stack থেকে সরবে না।

keyPoints.en: Linked stacks still need allocation-failure checks and cleanup.
keyPoints.bn: Linked stack-এও allocation failure যাচাই ও cleanup দরকার।

keyPoints.en: Bracket matching requires both correct types and nested order.
keyPoints.bn: Bracket মেলাতে শুধু সংখ্যা নয়, ধরন ও nesting-এর ক্রমও ঠিক চাই।

examQuestions.question: State the array-stack invariant and explain push/pop boundary checks.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Count is between zero and capacity and names the next free slot. Push requires count below capacity, writes at count and increments it. Pop requires count above zero, decrements it and reads that slot. Peek reads count−1 without changing count. Failed operations leave the stack and output unchanged.

examQuestions.question: Trace bracket matching for {[()]} and ([)].
examQuestions.answerHtml: The valid input pushes {, [ and (, then matches and pops ), ] and } in reverse order, ending empty. In ([)], the first closer ) meets [ at the top, so matching fails immediately even though total counts agree. At the end of otherwise valid scanning, any remaining opener also means failure.

examQuestions.question: Compare linked-stack ownership with array-stack storage.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The array owns a fixed inline buffer and changes a count without per-element allocation. The linked owner points to allocated nodes; push allocates and links, pop unlinks and frees, and cleanup frees all remaining nodes. Allocation failure must preserve the old top. Both represent the same LIFO operations.
